paragraphs: Overall credibility is unknown, so the results must not be described as converged or reliable. The mesh quality check for step s1 is unknown: second-order elements on curved surfaces became too distorted after upgrading, so straight-edge second-order elements were used and the curved surfaces are approximated by chords. Stresses near curved surfaces may therefore deviate noticeably.

Two other checks for step s1 passed. Reaction force balance holds, with external loads cancelled by support reactions. Mesh convergence of both maximum stress and maximum displacement passed across the three mesh levels. However, these passes do not offset the unknown mesh quality result.

The maximum von Mises stress away from constrained faces is {{s1.vm_max_mpa}}, and the maximum displacement is {{s1.u_max_mm}}. The material yield strength is {{s1.strength_mpa}}. The maximum stress over the three mesh levels is {{s1.conv2.level0}}, {{s1.conv2.level1}} and {{s1.conv2.level2}}. The maximum displacement is {{s1.conv3.level0}}, {{s1.conv3.level1}} and {{s1.conv3.level2}}.
No safety factor is given. The credibility checks did not pass (the conclusion is unknown), so the program does not provide one.

Modal step m1 gives the first four natural frequencies: {{m1.f1_hz}} ({{m1.f1_rpm}}), {{m1.f2_hz}} ({{m1.f2_rpm}}), {{m1.f3_hz}} ({{m1.f3_rpm}}) and {{m1.f4_hz}} ({{m1.f4_rpm}}). The model includes only the part's own mass and stiffness, so added mass is not accounted for. Supports are treated as ideal constraints, and real bearing stiffness would lower the frequencies.

Other limitations: the analysis is linear elastic with small deformation, with no contact, residual stress or surface hardening. Stresses near constrained and loaded faces come from idealized boundary conditions and were excluded from the maximum stress. Stresses at sharp corners grow with mesh refinement (a theoretical singularity) and should not be used directly as a design basis.
suggestions: Reduce the mesh size on the curved surfaces so that there are at least several element layers across them, then rerun the mesh quality check.
Have an engineer review the stresses near curved surfaces, since they may be inaccurate with chord-approximated geometry.
Do not use the sharp-corner stresses directly; add a fillet or verify the local stress with a dedicated local model or hot-spot method.
Add any attached masses to the model, and supply bearing stiffness data to refine the natural frequencies.
Rerun the credibility check after remeshing and request a safety factor only if the overall conclusion becomes a pass.
